<thought>We need the number of aromatic carbons. The best way is to obtain the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample and count the signals that fall in the typical aromatic carbon chemical shift range (≈110–160 ppm). This will give the count of distinct aromatic carbon environments, which corresponds to the number of aromatic carbons in the molecule (assuming no symmetry that makes equivalent carbons give a single signal). We'll request the carbon NMR spectrum and then count the aromatic-region peaks.</thought>
